The numbers

Nobody outside the AI companies can measure a single question exactly. So we start from what companies have published, add independent research, and always keep a low, middle and high estimate. Every number on the main page shows the whole range.

WhatLowMidHighUnit
Electricity per text answer · Wh0.240.341.86Wh
  • Google: "the median Gemini Apps text prompt uses 0.24 watt-hours (Wh) of energy" (Aug 2025; includes idle machines and data-centre overhead) · low · 2026-10-02
  • OpenAI (Sam Altman): "the average query uses about 0.34 watt-hours" (June 2025) · mid · 2026-10-02
  • MIT Technology Review: Llama 3.1 405B, "an estimated 6,706 joules total, for each response" · high · 2026-10-02 (Article estimates totals by doubling measured GPU energy.)
Electricity per AI picture · Wh0.631.222.9Wh
  • MIT Technology Review: Stable Diffusion 3 Medium 1024px, "an estimated 2,282 joules total" (low); "about 4,402 joules" at higher quality (mid) · low,mid · 2026-10-02 (Article estimates totals by doubling measured GPU energy.)
  • Luccioni, Jernite, Strubell, Power Hungry Processing (2023): "image generation, whose mean consumption is 2.9kWh" per 1,000 inferences · high · 2026-10-02
Electricity per short AI video (about 5 seconds) · Wh25.390944Wh
  • Delavande, Pierrard & Luccioni (Hugging Face), "Video Killed the Energy Budget" (2025), Table 4: CogVideoX-5B uses 21.6 Wh (GPU) + 2.4 Wh (CPU) + 1.3 Wh (RAM) for one 49-frame 480x720 clip · low · 2026-10-03 (single H100 GPU, no data-centre overhead; 25.3 Wh is the sum)
  • Same paper: "generating a single short video with WAN2.1–T2V–1.3B consumes nearly ∼90 Wh" · mid · 2026-10-03 (modern open model, ~5 s at 720p)
  • MIT Technology Review: older CogVideoX clip "about 109,000 joules" (low); newer five-second clip "about 3.4 million joules" (mid). No published figure for frontier video models, so high = mid. · high · 2026-10-02 (Article estimates totals by doubling measured GPU energy.)
  • Cross-check, same paper: "WAN2.1-T2V-14B consumes over 415 Wh" · high · 2026-10-03 (an independent measurement in the hundreds of Wh supports the high end)
Water used at the AI building (cooling) per kWh · L/kWh0.120.361.08L/kWh
  • Amazon: "global data center operations used just 0.12 liters of water per kilowatt-hour (L/kWh) in 2025" · low · 2026-10-02
  • Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, 2024 US Data Center Energy Usage Report (p. 48): "the overall average WUE, which stays just over 0.36 L/kWh through 2023" · mid · 2026-10-02
  • Google: the median text prompt "consumes 0.26 milliliters ... of water" for 0.24 Wh (= 1.08 L/kWh, our division) · high · 2026-10-02
Water used at power plants to make each kWh · L/kWh02.184.4L/kWh
  • Mytton, Data centre water consumption (npj Clean Water 2021): "The US average water intensity for electricity generation for 2015 was 2.18 litres per kilowatt hour" (mid); generation cooling "consumption ranging from 0.00 to 4.4 L/kWh ... depending on the system characteristics" (low, high) · low,mid,high · 2026-10-02
CO2 per kWh of electricity · gCO2/kWh125473560gCO2/kWh
  • Google: the median text prompt "emits 0.03 grams of carbon dioxide equivalent" for 0.24 Wh, using Google's 2024 fleetwide grid carbon intensity (= 125 g/kWh, our division) · low · 2026-10-02
  • Ember Global Electricity Review 2025: "Emissions intensity dropped by 2.3% to 473 grams of CO2 per kilowatt hour (gCO2/kWh)" in 2024 · mid · 2026-10-02
  • Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025: "China's carbon intensity of electricity generation was 560 gCO2/kWh, down 4.1% from 2023" · high · 2026-10-03 (a coal-heavy grid that hosts many data centres; location-based, 2024)

AI's share of data-centre electricity (United States, 2024) · share0.2650.320.38share
  • MIT Technology Review (citing Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory): "Data centers in the US used somewhere around 200 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2024" and "AI-specific servers in these data centers are estimated to have used between 53 and 76 terawatt-hours" (53/200 = 26.5%, 76/200 = 38%) · low,mid,high · 2026-10-02 (US 2024 share, used as our estimate for the world (no quotable global figure exists; the IEA shows one only in a chart). The world share is probably lower. Mid is the middle of the range.)
Growth in 2025 of electricity used by AI-focused data centres · share0.50.50.5share
  • IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI (2026): "Electricity consumption from AI-focused data centres grew even faster, surging 50% in 2025." · low,mid,high · 2026-10-03 (single published estimate)

AI's share of all data-centre electricity is the United States' 2024 share, 26.5–38%, used as our estimate for the world: nobody publishes a world figure in words. The real world share is probably lower.

How it grows, year by year

Sources publish only a few years: what data centres used in 2024 and 2025, and forecasts for 2030 and 2035. We fill in the years between with plain rules and mark every filled-in number as calculated. Where a source gives no low estimate, we say so instead of inventing one. Years after 2025 are forecasts.

Your privacy

  • No accounts, no cookies, no tracking scripts, and nothing loaded from other companies' servers.
  • The calculator runs in your browser. We never see what you enter.
  • Hum's first version saved a "world" on your device; the current site removes it the next time you visit.
